review_text: I never forgot my visit of the mine 45 years ago, It is just as awesome now. The mine has been in operation for 100 + years, but later this year, the operation will start going underground. The visit is free, but you must have a reservation as there is only ONE bus per day. You first stop at the old miners' town, (uninhabited since 2007) ; it would have been interesting to learn a bit more about the living conditions... I doubt they were as idyllic as they want you to believe! You also learn about the mining operation and then visit the actual sight: it is the largest open-air copper mine in the world. Make sure you wear shoes (no sandals allowed) and long sleeves. If you travel with children, ask about the age limit. At the end of the free visit, as "payment", be generous to the children's health clinic the mine sponsors.

review_text: The day started at 04:30 a we got up whilst is was still dark. We had booked a tour to the Tatio Geysers with Luna Dorada Tours as the owner/guide (Paul) spoke excellent English. We were collected at 05:00 and headed out of town and started climbing straight away through dirt roads that were heavily eroded in places. I started feeling unwell and thought I was taking a bug or had travel sickness. However on arrival at our destination I discovered when I left the bus I was dizzy and light headed and feeling very nauseous. The temperature was hovering around freezing and everyone was wrapped up and cold in the early morning. We walked very slowly to our first geyser - difficult to describe in words. It was bubbling and steaming with small spurts - not too high. As light started to appear in the sky, the geysers started to display the colours of the mineral elements - green, red, ochre. There was a slight sulphurous smell but not too strong. We walked through the geyser field - over 60 active geysers. This is the third largest geyser field on earth. Yellowstone is the largest, then one in Siberia then El Tatio. The morning light was spectacular as the rising sun glinted off snow covered volcanoes. After the walk I felt even worse. A light breakfast was served in the cold on a table beside the tour bus. All I could manage was some coco tea - coco leaves in hot water with a very mild narcotic stimulant meant to assist in altitude sickness. It made me feel worse. We climbed back on the bus and I was struggling to get sufficient oxygen. A short drive took us to the little pools filled with hot water (35 degrees Celsius) that you could enter. On leaving the bus this time I thought I was going to pass out - the nausea was so bad. The guide got assistance from someone else who gave me some drops to help - but they didn't make much difference. Sonia went for a dip in thenthermal spring but at this stage I was curled up in the bus feeling thoroughly miserable with myself. I dozed on and off during the next couple of hours as the bus made a couple of stops. The first was at an ancient settlement called Machuka where there are ruins dating from 1800 years ago. They had built a replica pueblo which looked a bit touristy. Sonia had a walk and took some photos. The next stop was at a lagoon with wild vicuñas and flamingoes. Another stop was to see a llama and there were lots more vicuñas. We started to descend and I started feeling more human again. The views through Cactus Valley were wonderful. These Cacti grow 1 cm per year - some of them are over 10 meters tall making them over 1000 years old. We were eventually dropped off at 12:30 and we collapsed into bed to catch up on some sleep.

review_text: The tour delivers exactly what it promised on paper, but with a safety-third, get-this-over-with attitude that really diminished our experience. We had changed to this company because our original company didn’t have helmets, while this one said it did. Imagine our surprise, then, to find that we were being herded onto the horses—there really is no other way to describe it—without helmets, and, when we asked about them (in Spanish), we were told it was too late. I will say this: the leaders were the real deal, with spurs, sombreros, and permanent scowls. They also did not speak a word of English, and none of the people on our tour were particularly fluent in Spanish. We traveled on an incredibly beautiful, incredibly narrow ridge with little margin for error. The leaders did not ask our names or give us theirs, and we only found out when we asked that Heather’s horse was named “trastornado” (deranged). It was an incredible site, and an incredible feeling, but each time the horses misstepped or startled, we saw our lives flash before our eyes. When we got to the top, three different groups converged there for stargazing with a telescope. There was a guide who spoke at length in Spanish about a number of constellations. The stars were astonishing, of course; that is the Pisco valley. It took some time for each person to look through the telescope, though, and after the first hour, most people seemed to lose interest. At the end, they took us back to the center of town, rather than their office, which is where they said I could leave my backpack. The backpack contained my breakfast, and it left me hangry. There are many tour companies in Pisco Elqui, all of whom can show off its glorious night sky. I see no reason to recommend Turismo Migrantes for the job. Dear Guests: Our team regrets the negative experience that you lived, because our goal is customer satisfaction. We want to answer the following aspects that you mentioned: 1- Use of helmet: the Chilean riding standard does not require the use of a helmet and our company performs in this traditional way, we deliver chupallas (Huaso hat) for daytime activities and we have multipurpose helmets in our agency which are handed out only when a customer request it. Considering the self-assurance and safety that helmets give to our customers while riding, we have considered making an acquisition for next season. 2- Guide did not speak English: Migrants Tourism has bilingual guides, in the first part of the tour that last 1 hour the local guide (a Huaso) does not speak English, but upon arrival at the astronomical scene there is a guide who speaks English and translates for you. 3- Route: We use alternative paths that have been used since ancient times by Huasos and mule drivers where they pass with animals in the foot hills of the mountain, although they are narrow roads, they are roads for horses and in 10 years of experience we have never had an accident. We also inform our passengers the characteristics of these roads so they can take the decision of going or not. Thanks for commenting your experience with us.

review_text: Booked a somewhat last minute W Trek with Chile Nativo in March of 2020. After a lot of research, I realized that while I COULD book the trek independently, there were a LOT of factors to consider and things that had to align perfectly to make it work. Logistically, there are TONS of details and I am so glad that I left it to experts to create for me. However, COVID happened and over the next two years, we would reschedule multiple times. Daniela from Chile Native was very communicative and always kept me in the loop on what my options were and answered my endless questions. The day before the trek, we met Alicia for orientation at Chile Nativo in Puerto Natales. She provided a map, vouchers for all the services, lunch for the next day (that sandwich was DELICIOUS) and walked us through all the details of what to expect throughout the trip. She provided tips on many options throughout the trek (Mirador Britanico, Hanging bridges), including taking the Lago Skottsberg trail to Paine Grande that is unmarked when going east to west. It was a highlight of our trek. To answer two questions: Should you use an outfitter to plan your W Trek? 100% yes - there are so many details to planning a successful trip - not just refugios/campsites, but buses and ferries - I am sure I would have missed something and been very distressed. Leave it to the experts and lean on them. Patagonia is very challenging logistically for many reasons. Even as a planner, I really appreciated their help and expertise. Should you use Chile Nativo? 100% yes. They were helpful and went above and beyond for me. I would not hesitate to use them again or to recommend them to friends. Review of: W Trek Torres del Paine

review_text: You will quickly leave the port and make your way up to the charms of the Vicente Perez National Park. Do not fret if it is misty as this is a common occurrence in this region and it will clear before the action starts. Firstly, you will pass through picturesque Puerto Varas on the shores of Lake Llanquihue known as the 'City of Roses' which is a lovely settlement influenced by German migrants 150 years ago and now is a popular tourist gateway to Chile's Lake District. Great for lunch and shopping later. Soon you will be following the course of the Petrohue River and visiting its Falls before reaching the enchanting Lake Esmeralda renowned for its exquisite emerald coloured waters, green forested steep slopes and the highlight of this tour, the Mt Fuji of Chile, the dormant Volcano Osorno which is just magnificent. It is everybody's idea of the perfect volcano in shape, snow-capped as well and serenely forming the backdrop to this beautiful lake as you cruise its waters on a catamaran. Chile at its stunningly best and just unforgettable. Its a must and you will have your camera out so many times you will be glad you charged it up before this trip. Enjoy.

review_text: We booked five tours through PatagoniaShorex but only two were worth the fee charged. Jaime, the owner, met us in Puerto Montt, Chile. His tour was fine. But the tours he 'booked' for us in Punta Arenas, Chile; Punte del Este, Uruguay and Buenos Aires, Argentina were VERY DISAPPOINTING. For example, we arranged (and paid for) a 'custom/combination' tour in Punta Arenas. The guide at the pier had the wrong (customer) name on his placard and once WE found HIM he had no idea what we had booked. He was not knowledgeable at all, spoke very little about the country, scenery, history. Nice kid, but not well prepared for this type of tour. A taxi ride would have been just fine at a fraction of the cost. In Punte del Este, once again we had a 'guide' who did not guide as spoke very little about anything. He simply dropped us off at various points and brought us back after only 2 1/2 hours (we paid for four). Once again, a taxi would have been just fine at a fraction of the cost. In Buenos Aires our driver was again, quiet. He was courteous enough, but spoke very little on the VERY LONG drive to and from the "ranch" in the pampas. Regardless of the weather the drive was far longer than advertised at PatagoniaShorex. Once we arrived at the ranch access road we stood there for another 35 minutes waiting for pickup by another vehicle. The drive to/from the ranch took up another hour out of our day. The ranch was pretty enough, but the experience was quite disappointing: no gauchos (due to weather), no folklorico dancers (as promised) and the lunch was also disappointing. We did have email communication with Jaime throughout our trip and all he said was 'sorry'. At one point he mentioned 'compensation' but no refund was offered. We do not recommend this business for ANY port other than Porto Montt, Chile. These were not tour guides, they were taxi drivers. Ugh... review_text: There are many vineyard tours to choose from when staying in Santiago. The grapes the vineyard use come from various regions around Chile (1800 hectares) but there are only a few at this vineyard largely for the tourists! Very photogenic. There were several fermentation vats. Very modern looking. But the cellars where the wine is aged in oak barrels were much older. As with all wine tours, it ended with some tasting. All very nice. But after that we were taken to the aromas room. So many familiar smells, but hard to identify them without looking at the label. The bad smells to avoid were cork, sulphur, vinegar and mould. I am sure I have had wine in the past that had some of these smells! But honestly, this was good fun trying to guess the aroma. We were hopeless..... review_text: We arrived in Valparaiso via cruise ship on Nov 8th and needed a transfer to Santiago. We, six friends in total, were in no hurry to get to Santiago and wanted to explore Valparaiso and then stop at some wineries en-route to our hotel in Santiago. Esteban helped us tailor the perfect day tour for us. Our driver, Hector and tour guide, Jeannette picked us up at the pier in a comfortable van for the six of us. We started the day with an amazing tour of Valparaiso. Jeannette was very knowledgeable and well informed. We then headed out towards Santiago and a snack was provided for our road trip. We were very pleased that they paid attention to detail and made sure that the snacks took into consideration the dietary needs of 2 of our friends. The wineries we selected were amazing and Jeannette made sure we were well accommodated. We did end up hitting rush hour in Santiago and we felt so sorry for Hector, but he handled it like a champ and was very patient. Once we arrived in our room, we realized that we had left a bag at the pier. It was late in the day and we called both the cruise ship and Esteban. Esteban came to our rescue and our bag was delivered to our hotel room the following day at the same time our cruise ship returned our call from the night before. If it was not for Esteban and his assurance that he would retrieve the bag, we probably would not have enjoyed our first full day in Santiago. Thank you Private Tours Santiago for ensuring our wonderful vacation ended on a high note!

review_text: We had four days in Santiago and we were keen to get outside of the city centre and do some Maipo Valley wine tasting. We've toured wineries before so we were looking for something different and were excited to find La Bicicleta Verde's Bike and Wine tour - an awesome opportunity to explore a vineyard by bike as well as learn about the wine production process and taste some of the final products. The vineyard, Cousiño Macul, is easily reached by metro and a short taxi ride, or an uber from the city. The tour involves a leisurely bike ride of around 45 minutes to an hour through the vineyards of the Macul estate. It's a beautiful, scenic place with the Andes mountains on one side, and views of Santiago city on the other. We stopped halfway through the ride to taste a Rosé before getting back on the bikes to explore some more. The green bikes were in decent condition and the ride itself was very easy: mostly flat and with plenty of stops along the way. Back at the winery, the tour visits the winery production area and then the impressive original underground barrel cellars. Then it's on to three more tastings of Cousiño Macul wines. The wine bar on site sells wine by the glass if you're keen to try some more wines after the tour, and of course you can also buy bottles to take with you. Our guide Sarah was lovely, engaging and full of interesting information about the history of wine in Chile, Cousiño Macul and the wine production process. She also did a fantastic job of taking us through the see-smell-sip wine tasting experience. We had a small group of 5 for the English speaking tour, and though there was a second, larger Spanish-speaking tour group leaving around the same time as us, we didn't see them during our bike ride or winery tour. We did the 11am tour, which finished around 2pm, giving us time to head to another local winery for more tastings. Sarah also recommended some local lunch spots. We really enjoyed our experience with La Bicicleta Verde and would absolutely recommend the bike and wine tour as a great way to break up a city visit to Santiago and try some great Chilean wine. Hola Twofortheworld! Thank you so much for your exhaustive review and 5 stars. I am glad our values of being casual and fun are appreciated by the travelers that come to bike with us. Sarah is a lovely human and a perfect guide, she knows her stuff and she loves to share! We do what we love and love what we do here at La Bicicleta Verde, and part of the reason of this is that we can be our self around you guys and show off the places we love so much. I hope you enjoy the rest of your stay, and if you make it through to Santiago come say hey to the Green Team at our Base near Bellas Artes. Sincerely, Peter.

review_text: We were very disappointed in the content of the Coyhaique City Tour, especially when comparing its $155pp US cost to that of excursions we took in Puerto Montt, Stanley, Ushuaia and elsewhere that were as much as half the price but much richer in content. Our guide, Luca (sp?), a Coyhaique native, was a genial and knowledgeable young man who did the best he could with what he had to work with, but he and his community simply don’t have a lot to display to visitors like us, based on what we saw. It was a long drive from the port to the city of Coyhaique and when we arrived we were advised 1) there weren’t a lot of shops or restaurants open because it was Saturday and 2) we would spend about 20 minutes here before heading back in the direction we came to stop for lunch at a local ranch. The lunch stop at the ranch was the unique experience of the tour but while it was interesting to see how the lamb asado was prepared, the food was mediocre and we were crammed into a barn-like dining hall so tightly the people at the table behind us had to completely leave their table for us to have enough room to exit, ourselves. If a qualified U.S. fire marshal saw the situation they’d cite them for operating a dangerous establishment. On the way back, the guide made a suggestion to stop for photos at what I can only describe as a dead tree swamp. None of the passengers were interested and if I’d bothered to take a picture I’d share it here so you could see why. It was a swamp with dead tree stumps, but that’s apparently what qualified as a place of interest on this escapade. In short, don’t waste your $$ on this tour - certainly not at the $155pp price. I wish we’d given more credence to some of the less-flattering reviews we read and bypassed it, ourselves.

review_text: I would not recommend this company. We were with a group from a cruise, gathered from Facebook and Cruise Critic. First the good. We ended up off the ship an hour late, and that was not their fault, but the ships. Our guide was good, and asked us what we wanted to sacrifice. We said lunch. So we were doing the volcano and the falls. On the whole Ricardo, the guide did a good job. The volcano visit was good, but halfway down the mountain, the brakes on the bus failed. This is inexcusable for a tour company. We don't know if it was the bus or that our driver didn't know how to use engine braking, but in any case that was not part of what we paid for. The guide than asked us for water to cool it down. Very unprofessional. We also had 3 hours to get back to the port, so it was stressful. After about 35 minutes we were on our way. However that made the falls (which were more rapids than falls, but I understand it was the time of year, I just wish they'd told us that before we drove there) visit short. On the way back, the guide wanted to stop at the town of Puerto Varas, but we were already pushing time (we wanted to arrive 30 minutes before last tender), so we did a drive by. We ended up driving through the town, rather than straight to the dock, but there was no narration of guiding, we just looked out the window. Total waste of time. We had two buses. Friends on the other bus reported their guide didn't speak English well. Review of: Full-Day Osorno Vulcano and Petrohue Falls Small-Group Tour Dear Abby We have reviewed, analyzed and verified with the driver and guide his comment, which does not conform to reality, for the following reasons 1.- The delay in the pick up was 2 hours, we waited for you at the port at 7 am and the last person to disembark was at 9:00 am, the time the tour began 2.- The ship removed 2 hours of permanence in port, which initially was from 07:00 a.m. to 05:00 p.m., lowering the return time to 03:00 p.m., for which the group decided to return at 02:00 p.m., this produced that there would be no detention for lunch and that there would only be a panoramic visit to Puerto Varas, all of this discussed with the group and agreeing with the entire group In these 2 points the agency has no responsibility because the tour adjusts to the ship's times and that was stipulated at the time of contracting the service 3.- You say that the guide was unprofessional, but you also say that the guide did a good job, so you contradict yourself, he never asked for water to cool off 4.- The stop of the bus was made as a precaution when noticing something strange, so it is known that a stone entered the area of the wheels, which produced unusual heating of the wheel, the water was used to lower the temperature and remove the stone, it was only 15 minutes, the group continued the tour with the same bus, there was no need to change, because it was only a preventive stop, we use new buses, the oldest is from 2020 and is fully maintained up to date and are reviewed periodically. These events could have happened to any vehicle Although it is true that constructive criticism helps us to improve and is received very well by our agency, in this case I only see bad intention on your part, this comment will only create harm to our agency At the end of the tour, the rest of the group applauded the guide and even thanked him with a tip for his work

review_text: We had a perfect day to trek into the Andes - imagine that wide open space, the mountains, snow and perfect blue sky - the best day ever, and the best experience of our trip to Chile. Pickup was right on time with Diego, Felipe and Coti in a comfortable van that fit 11 hikers and our guides. We made a stop at a local roadside inn for breakfast and bathrooms, then back on the road - about 2 1/2 hours total to our final destination. The start of the climb was not easy - you are at a high elevation to start and the trail is rocky and steep. Not exactly for the faint of heart, but well worth the effort. Be sure to have sunscreen, a hat and a camera. Long pants are advisable as the sticker bushes (not a technical term!) were abundant. Also abundant - the views - absolutely gorgeous everywhere you look! I was hoping to see/photograph some condors, and we did see one juvenile bird, plus a few lizards, some goats, horses and other birds. The group split after lunch with some heading back to the van for a trip to the hot springs and 4 of us continuing on with Coti to hike the valley and get up close to the glaciers. We had fun crossing the water several times, including removing our shoes at a particularly wide spot, but we were all up for the adventure! Coti gave us background on the ecosystem, history on the valley and how it was formed - she was very informative. It was clear she was concerned about seeing the area protected for the future. Review of: Andes Day Volcano 8K - Cajón del Maipo Dear Karin!! It was so lovely to meet you. We enjoy a lot sharing our knowledge about the area and having conversations with our visitors. That was an adventourous day for sure! Hugs! Coti

review_text: Was a little uncertain about doing this as it was towards the end of my trip and money was a little tight. Very, very glad I did. In a trip where cities merged into similarity and travelling between destinations was long and tiring, this was invigorating, inspiring and thoroughly enjoyable. With (myself) only having a basic grasp of what's going on up there, Jorge could have written for the Cosmos TV show, such was his informative and enjoyable basic timeline of night-time discovery. After the introduction we were treated to a feast of tasty warm/cold food and an unnecessarily (in a good way) wide variety of hot drinks. After the feast, we started moving through the array of telescopes Jorge has on-site. To the naked eye alone, I've never seen a more impressive nightsky. With Jorge's equipment, knowledge and direction we were able to see countless galaxies (as many as nine in one viewport) and multiple other planets and formations. Once I arrived at the location, I never thought again about the money I'd spent, only how grateful I was for the experience and how I wish I knew more about our cosmos. review_text: Sebastian Bueno ruined our Torres del Paine Trekking Experience tour on 1st March 2024 because he was in a rush to return for the beer festival in Puerto Natales. If you do tours with W Circuit Patagonia (we did 2 tours) you will get no explanation of the area and will have limited time at key attractions. Their tours are just overpriced transport to the Torres del Paine national park. The bus is only 10USD from Puerto Natales. I was aware that we had 9 hours for the hike so I hiked at the correct pace. Unfortunately our guide Sebastian Bueno wanted to return quickly for the beer festival so he set a very fast pace. I spent almost the entire hike alone, arriving at 12:20 at the top (10 minutes behind the group). The weather was cloudy and rainy when I arrived at the top, with no view of the towers. However, I wanted to wait 1 hour to have a chance of seeing the towers. At 12:30 Sebastian said that we had to go down because the weather was bad. I explained that I had just arrived and wanted some time to rest and wait for the weather. He got angry with me and said "This is not a private tour. You should not be on this tour if you don't want to follow the group. You should book a private tour instead.". This mad me angry so I refused to leave. The group left without a view of the towers. I remained until 13:25, getting a full view of the towers. After finishing the trek, on time within 9 hours, I had a chance to chat to some of the group and shared my photos. They then realised their experience had been ruined by Sebastian Bueno because he put the beer festival before his job. Sebastian Bueno should not be working as a tour guide because he does not care about the customer experience. He just does the minimum work required. To W Circuit Patagonia: Please don't allow your tour guides to ruin the experience for customers. We spend a lot of money and time to travel to Patagonia so should be treated with respect.

review_text: A great valley for winery hopping, tasting, learning, scenery and food. It may be a little difficult to get from winery to winery, however you can rent a driver for the day who will take you anywhere you need to go. Also there are some tours available that will bring you to more than one winery. I highly recommend the Viu Manent winery, it was my favourite. Their wine is cheap and of impeccable quality. Tours can be done is English and are done on horse and carriage. The staff is great and lots of fun and really go out of the way to make your stay unique. A small cafeteria is located outside with small and fine foods. It was really my favourite winery (this coming from someone who went to more wineries in Chile than can be remembered). I went back 3 times. If you can go into the town, there is a museum there that covers a bunch of different themes and is really well laid out, the famous hotel that is attached to it is famous for it's brunch. If you love wine and can appreciate the amazing scenery, I highly recommend spending some time in this area.

review_text: This was a super trip and a great way to see the mountains outside of Santiago. From start to finish the tour was well organized. review_text: We booked a private 4 day 3 night tour of Salar de Uyuni with Cruz Andina in advance and made a deposit (even though a number of internet sites cautioned against doing both), requested Andres Valencia as a guide (oxymoronically, based on internet recommendations), crossed our fingers and flew to South America. At the Cruz Andina office in San Pedro de Atacama Raul helped us though the intricacies of visiting Bolivia (more complicated than we imagined without a pre-arranged visa), and arranged local tours to replace the schedule botched by a local hotel (more on that elsewhere). The local tours were farmed out to other local agencies (a common practice in town) and were great. The tour itself was all we had hoped for. The sights and experiences were exceptional. The food and accommodations were basic but as good as to be had in the area (this is not the Champagne region of France). Andres was superb from the start. An overbearing Bolivian border official scrutinized our US dollars intended to pay for our Visas, frowned and pronounced two hundred dollar bills unfit. Yes, they were folded multiple times but were unblemished and devoid of any tears; yet they were” rejects”. Having no other cash we though that Bolivia was not going to happen. In stepped Andres, telling us not to worry and off we drove. Somehow, he fixed things. Andres followed though similarly the rest of the trip. He fixed everything; did everything necessary and more to ensure a wonderful trip. He was kind, friendly, knowledgeable and accommodating at every turn. It is not easy to be a (very safe) driver, local guide, cook, butler, trip coordinator, and DJ (we bonded over 60s music). Andres performed every role perfectly. Cruz Andina and Andres Valencia are both highly recommended.

review_text: We've just come off the Eden Navimag ferry, Puerto Natales to Puerto Montt. I've just been reading some of the reviews posted before me and I've got to say that they are generally pretty fair both the good ones and the bad ones. However if you don't find the worst ones hilarious then you really shouldn't consider taking Navimag. There is a lack of attention to detail which leaves it pretty rough around the edges but the crew are delightful and do their best to make the journey as comfortable as possible. The AAA cabins are small but functional and the food tends towards the lower end of school dinners but is available in large quantities and seems to be greatly appreciated by the lorry drivers who put away vast quantities of it. We did have a problem with toilet blockages which were out of action on our deck for 24 hours while the on board plumber removed nappies, toys, even a t-shirt that had been introduced to the system by the less intelligent passengers (or perhaps unsupervised children). This may make the ticket price seem exorbitant but there are two things that make it all completely worthwhile. The first is the indescribably beautiful scenery in this unspoilt wilderness. This is enhanced by the great lectures given by the very enthusiastic onboard naturalist, Percy.The second is the type of people who are attracted to a more eccentric form of travel. On our journey they came from all over the world and were students travelling on a shoestring, early retired people getting off the beaten track and a few families. I suspect what we all had in common is that we would find the idea of travelling on a large posh cruise liner totally alarming! This is predominantly a cargo ship so don't rely on the published time-table being followed. Save yourself any stress and allow at least 24 hours for running late, even in good weather. We absolutely loved the journey. Even with its faults it was a very special experience. I would recommend this journey if your comfort zone extends well beyond the mainstream; otherwise you may prefer to wait 18 months or so until Navimag's brand new ferry is launched.

review_text: I absolutely LOVED my tours with this company! HIGHLY RECOMMEND! I did one tour wine tasting in Casablanca valley and another tour exploring the Andes Mountains both during my visit to Santiago de Chile. For these tours my friend and I were picked up by our driver, Miguel, and tour guide, Fernando. Both Miguel and Fernando were very nice, fun, knowledgeable and easy going. They really made us feel comfortable and enjoy ourselves. For the wine tasting in Casablanca valley we went to three wineries that were all beautiful! We took tours at each winery and then got to taste the wine at the end. If you enjoy wine, especially sauvignon blancs and pinot noirs, then you will love this day! For the tour of the Andes, we went to Valle Nevado which is an amazing ski resort. If you like to ski or snowboard and you are here in the winter, this place is a MUST. I am not big on skiing, so we just walked around this area and then went to another mountain town for some winter activities! I did ziplining and a “panoramic view” lift where I got to see amazing views of the mountains. We also made a stop along the mountain to set up a table for some cheese, crackers and wine! During both of these tours, Fernando took lots of photos of my friend and me with his professional camera. Both of these tours were highlights of my trip to Santiago de Chile!

We continued with the cable car ride to the top of a hill where you have an observatory (working in the evening) and a small village representing the 3 most important cultures of Chile (Mapuche, Aymara and Rapa Nui). The view is really fantastic. We had then a visit to the plant and cellars and tasted the different wines of the place. To finalize our visit, we had lunch in the restaurant of the vinery. Muchas gracias por sus comentarios. Nuestra Viña consta con un Museo del Automóvil, tour por la Viña, recorrido en teleférico en donde se pueden recorrer diferentes replicas de Aldeas indigenas. review_text: Constitution Square is a lovely plaza in the heart of Santiago’s Civic district. It is surrounded by government buildings, including La Moneda, the Presidential Palace. The plaza dates to 1935 and owes its current design to a 1984 renovation. Here’s your chance for a photo of the Chilean flag – 12 of them flank the Palace entrance where the changing of the guard takes place. Four monuments of national Chilean figures anchor the plaza (see if you can find the one with the bullet hole). We enjoyed a quiet walk in Constitution Square on a late Sunday afternoon. This is a great place to experience Chilean history.

review_text: I went on the Tour Astronomico from San Pedro de Atacama. It was a waste of time. Firstly, it was a night of an almost full moon and so the bulk of the stars were invisible. When I booked the tour I was not told warned about this and given the option to book another night. I was part of a group that had two guides, one for Spanish and one for English. There were five of us with the English guide but unfortunately we couldn't hear what he was saying because the Spanish guide was almost shouting with his group. The constellation of Orion was pointed out using a laser pen as were Venus, Mars and Jupiter. All of these are easily visible from Europe, so nothing was learned there. When we looked through the telescopes, nothing could be seen clearly, not even the moon. When it was time for the food, we arrived at the table to find what amounted to be the food left over from a previous group. Finally, at the end of the evening a photographer took pictures of individuals with the sky as the background. When I received these two days later they were out of focus! I have complained to the company but as yet, nearly a week later, I have had no response.

review_text: Found this little aquarium in Valparaiso and thought why not. I was very disappointed in this place to able to call them self an aquarium is really a shame. Granted with a kid you can kill a bit of time, but don't take the whole family. 6500peso with a 15% discount was way to much to pay to see the 12 fish tanks which were no bigger than my fish tank back home. They have a touching pool at the end, however they don't teach good environmental respect by taking the various species out of the water to handle. None of the "fish tanks" (enclosures) replicate The Eco systems the fish are from. The fish have no where to hide (wait they have a pirate ship in one tank which I think came from one of their kids home aquariums). I understand that sometimes things start if small then grow, but this place lacks the most important part of modern sustainability....!.!.!. The part where you replicate the Eco system so that the species can feel less stress in their already stressful environment and to teach people about their Eco systems by seeing and exploring them.

review_text: I was looking forward to this part of my trip more than any other part and it did not disappoint in the slightest. You can see more stars than you could ever imagine, as it is one of the best places in the entire world to see stars due to the altitude, lack of smog, and lack of light pollution. My tour first used a laser pointer to point out constellations and teach you some basics, then set up huge telescopes to look at Jupiter, Saturn, specific stars, and nebula, and then ended with a Q&A where the guide answered all our complicated questions (alternate life forms, black holes, etc.) with impressive clarity. A great experience overall that you really can't miss.

review_text: I wanted to arrange a custom-designed tour to suit my personal interests. As I don't speak/read Spanish, I found it very hard to find information about rodeos being held in the area. I contacted Juan to ask if he could arrange a private tour to the rodeo at Maullin. Juan was very helpful in finding the details and booking with Juan was an easy process as he was prompt and thorough in answering my questions. He arrived on time to collect me from my accommodation and the vehicle was very clean and new. He was friendly and chatted about the local area as we travelled to the rodeo. The rodeo was such a wonderful experience, a very unique and authentic way to experience the traditions of Chile. Juan explained everything that was happening, and I felt welcome and part of the event. Travelling by myself with Juan, I felt safe the whole day. Juan also spoke to one of the huasos and I was very excited to be able to have a short ride on the the huaso's horse!! It was amazing to watch the pairs of huasos and their horses competing, the horses were in beautiful condition and were well-trained and responsive to their trainers. After watching the competition, Juan organised a traditional meal for lunch. Thank you, Juan, for helping me experience this exciting day, it was a day that I won't forget! review_text: My husband and I did the colchugua valley and the next day did the Casablanca valley. The colchugua valley was quite far but worth trekking to. We checked out 3 wineries in the Apalta Valley and loved the experience at all 3. Our favorite was the 2nd stop at Neyen. Delicious wines, great host, and beautiful scenery. The wine in this region was a little pricier than Casablanca but also better for us since we really enjoy reds! The Casablanca region was definitely chillier especially in the morning. We really liked the 2nd winery here too. They had a small operation and operated out of shipping containers which was unique! Host/sommelier was fabulous and fun! View was incredible! And who doesn’t like starting a tour with a glass of rose in hand?!?!!! Vivi and Jose were our guides and both super knowledgeable and accommodating. The one thing we learned was they do not ship wine back to the US. Sounds like the US has made this harder in the last couple years. I just wish I would’ve known before the tour so we could’ve brought the proper luggage to haul the wine back since we enjoy buying wines from new places, especially the kind of bottles you can’t find in the US. Thankfully we got back around 5:30PM on the Casablanca day (2nd day) and went to a few wine shops in the mall. The first place did not sell anything that made it conducive to ship 7bottles back. Then we went to a store called CAV that had the bubble wrap for each individual bottle (one time use) and they gave us a free 12 bottle box. Checked it with our luggage on the plane. Our hotel gave us some box tape and hopefully it arrives without issues in the US. So lesson learned, if you plan on buying wine, figure out how you will ship it back so you aren’t scrambling like we had to!

review_text: Spoiler Alert: Ben & Patagonia Line helped make this one of best days I've ever had on the water. Not being familiar with the area, my wife and I chose his service based on the other reviews on TripAdvisor. In the end, we were not disappointed and can affirm all the good things others have said about him here. Breaking down our day: Pre-trip: In the weeks leading up to our trip, Ben was extremely responsive and helpful via email. He made it a point to ask about my preferences, goals for the trip, etc and lived up to his word about trying to personalize the experience. Equipment: high quality gear from Simms and Reddington Location: breathtaking stretch of water on of the local estancias, draped against the Patagonian mountains (see pictures). plenty of wildlife, and no other anglers to boot! On the water: Ben was a patient, relaxed guide who helped me read the water, select high yield stretches and ultimately got me into fish quickly (and often). Very knowledgeable, and able to 'teach to the learner' by adapting his style from me (more experienced angler) to my wife (enthusiastic, but new to the sport). Lunch: a very high quality spread with steak, vegetables, wine, local brews, and other refreshments; what a treat to have lunch in the foothills with the mountains ahead of me and with no sounds but the water around me Transportation: timely, easy pick-up and drop-off Given the chance, I'd definitely fish with Ben again. In addition to high quality service and expertise as a guide, he also clearly brings a love for the land and sport of fishing to his work. A persistently curious person, I peppered him with him about everything from the history of fishing there to the local fauna to surrounding geography and ecology. From his answers, I could tell he is very connected and invested in the area -- to me, a critical quality that distinguishes good and great guides.

review_text: This was my first ever wine tour and I absolutely loved it! The winery was about an hour long bus ride away from Santiago. On the bus ride there, our tour guide gave us history and information about Santiago and Chile. He spoke both Spanish and English and was very easy to understand and converse with. The bike tour itself was a lot of fun! The bikes were comfortable and the pace of the tour was very good. The terrain was dirt and gravel roads. The vineyard itself was absolutely beautiful. We rode our bikes to different parts of the vineyard to learn about the grapes and taste them. We also saw some llamas and alpacas on the property, and got to see where the wine is fermented and stored. We had one wine tasting while riding our bikes (at a pavilion) and then 3 more wine tastings back at the main Santa Rita building. We also learned some history about the Santa Rita property during the Chilean fight for independence (story of the Santa Rita 120). After the wine tastings, we had time in the gift shop and then rode the bus back to Santiago. Overall it was a very enjoyable tour and the highlight of my weekend in Santiago.

review_text: My husband and I stayed at Estancia Mercedes for one night on our trip to Chile - directly after our three day trek in Torres del Paine. The entire family is so welcoming and warm and they were all truly open to sharing their life and special place with us. We arrived in the late afternoon so had time to rest up (for me) and catch some salmon (for my husband) in the beautiful lake in front of the house. Dinner the first night was amazing - a special zucchini bake, fresh clams, and salads straight from the greenhouse. On day 2 we started the day milking Guapa (harder than it looks!), enjoying a fresh breakfast, and then off on a horseback ride along the lake. The scenery was amazing and the horses were very friendly. Along the way we (or our gaucho leaders) rounded up some of the cows that were roaming around and brought them back for our lesson in marking the calves. Do this. Afterwards we were rewarded by a feast for lunch! We had such a special and memorable time at the Estancia - it was especially wonderful to meet the family and see how close they are to each other and to the land. I sincerely hope to return to Estancia Mercedes someday and to create some of the peace and happiness that exists in the place in my own life! Location is a 10, Hospitality is a 10! Hola Suzanne ¡¡¡ muchas gracias por tus hermosas palabras ¡¡¡ espero que el bebé esté bien después de tanto viaje. Nosotros la verdad quedamos muy contentos con su simpatía, su risa y su entusiasmo por todo lo que le ofrecimos hacer. Nos encantó tenerlos en nuestra casa, practicar un poco de inglés y sus vidas. Nuestro hogar estará abierto para ustedes siempre. Abrazos desde Patagonia. Sebastián y Familia :)

Negative points: when leaving the hotel in Atacama towards the border with Bolivia, the agency sent us a driver who was very sick (and who could have worn a mask during the journey). review_text: I strongly recommend not to hire this agency if you wish to have a good experience during your stay in san pedro de Atacama. On Wednesday we booked two places to the puritama baths for the Saturday morning, with the idea of relaxing for the few days of vacation, we pay both the tour and the entrance in advance via transfer. On Friday at 7 PM, we received a call saying that the tickets had sold out, we were surprised because he had confirmed the purchase on our face two days ago, he gave us as an excuse that the page was collapsed, immediately we told him that as it was possible if he was already supposed to have made the purchase two days earlier, then the page was collapsed for two days?? At this they admitted that they had really forgotten to buy them (i.e. they are liars and irresponsible) and offered to change the day to Sunday afternoon, which was impossible as that day we were traveling back home. Finally we had to run to see if we could book at another agency and it turns out that the page was not collapsed at all, but if they had sold out during the last minutes. In the end it was very stressful, we missed the opportunity to know the place we wanted and asked for the return of the money, we were told that during the night we made the return, which did not happen. We had to go back to the agency the next day in the evening to lobby and we just got paid back and cash! The administration are liars and irresponsible, never again! review_text: We booked the TAT Traditional Astronomical Tour and it was amazing! It lasted at least 4 hours: 2 hours of astronomical class and 2 hours observation with some of Jorges many telescopes. The astronomical class was very interesting and informative about the night sky and the history of astronomy. Jorge can answer any question! After the two hours class we could watch the sky with some telescopes. Jorge will align them to some star formation and then everyone can look through. After some time Jorge will realign them if the star formation has moved out of sight. The snack was in between the two sections of the tour and was really delicious. Jorges wife made some sandwiches, other snacks and multiple hot and cold drinks to warm up after the class. IMPORTANT: Contact Jorge at the beginning or before your trip because Jorge is a full time tourist guide and needs sometimes some time to reply to messages. Also, he can obviously do only one tour per night, so you need to be a bit flexible for your wish, but Jorge does everything he can to make it happen! Also, after sunset it gets really fast really cold in the Atacama desert, so bring warm clothes. If it's still too cold Jorge has some blankets and gas heaters for the astronomical class. I would definitely take the tour again when I come back to San Pedro de Atacama some time and would recommend it to everyone visiting San Pedro de Atacama! In addition, we had the chance to ask Jorge some of our general questions about the Atacama desert and he answered every question detailed and interesting. He knows his stuff perfectly as he grew up in this area. Therefore, I would also recommend him as a day-trip guide!

review_text: Have you ever done water slides in the theme park? You’ll experience similar emotions but it will be much cooler and much more fun. Imagine rafting on a beautiful river with a view of mountains. And, of course, a sense of achievement that comes for dessert. Me and my husband had 0 rafting experience and worried because we knew the waves would not be a joke at Futaleufu. But when I texted the manager of this company, he confirmed that this tour “bridge to bridge section” was suitable for beginners. And that was true! No, it was not an easy boring relaxing activity - we did have 4+ class waves and fast stream but the river was safe and without big stones. That’s why it’s suitable for beginners in my opinion. Even if you fall out of the raft, what will happen? Nothing. You’ll just have a cold bath haha. But nothing horrible or scaring. We didn’t even fall out of the raft and the raft didn’t flip. And, frankly, even if it did flip or we fell down, it would be fine because the river was safe and not deep anyway. We had soooo much fun during the whole activity, so much adrenaline. I couldn’t stop laughing and screaming like if I was in the theme park. At the end I decided to jump into the river because I felt so happy and excited. I didn’t even care that it was cold. And this is something I also recommend you to do when you’ll do this tour. Our guide, Vlad, was exceptional. I cannot imagine a more perfect guide and trust me I had many guides before in other places. No one can compare. review_text: The park is beautiful but not extraordinary, with nature representative of the area. You have to be lucky to make sightings of huemules and fauna in the sector. The trails do not represent a greater technical difficulty, and if you usually do trekking they are easier to tackle (long distances but on almost flat terrain and with steep but very short ascents - depending on the direction in which the route is taken -, descents steep dirt slopes and short passes through places exposed to falls in case of losing balance). The most popular trail (Los Carpinteros) is equipped with viewpoints of the lake and stairs in areas with difficult passage. The camping area is one of the most beautiful I have been to in a national park in Chile. It is well equipped, has a dishwasher, shared bathrooms and showers (with hot water) and multiple garbage cans. Each camping site has its own kitchen area that protects from the wind. Keep in mind that you can only pay with cash and there is no discount with the INJUV.

review_text: I accidentally gave the tour guide ~70USD because I had just arrived in Santiago from Argentina and I confused the denomination of the orange notes (20000 pesos and not 2000). I was intending to leave 16000 (10000 + 6000). I contacted them a few hours later to point out my mistake and kindly ask if by any chance I could get a partial refund on their good will because of an honest mistake. As a backpacker, I was travelling on a rather tight budget. They could have given a negative answer in many different ways, that I would have understood and accepted. Instead, they opted to send a very aggressive response, making up a story where I was trying to scam them, accusing me of being unethical and, effectively, a liar. And, of course, keeping all the money. Despite this shocking treatment, I responded with a very respectful response appealing to reason but I was plainly ignored for weeks. I believe this behaviour is very telling of what kind of people they are, and what kind of business they run beyond the friendliness of the guides. The tour itself was actually very good, I really enjoyed it and I am sad that this experience undermined it.

review_text: After spending a semester in Valparaíso, my friend and I had the most genuine experience and ate the best food we had eaten in 6 months during this cooking class. Chef Gonzalo Vial picked us up outside of Cafe Vinilo at around 11:30 and drove us to the market in Valparaíso. First of all, just getting the opportunity to see the distinct, beautiful markets that this city has to offer was an experience in itself - we saw huge rooms full of buckets of herbs and spices, and streets lined with fruit, vegetable, and fish vendors. Then he drove us through the hills of Valparaíso, pointing out some of the important yet less well-known buildings of the area, introducing us to his favorite Chilean music, and stopping to buy empanadas from his favorite empanada place. Then we went right to his home, where we briefly met his wonderful family. We worked in his kitchen for 5 1/2 hours. He insists that we prepare everything - he was a good teacher, patient, and we learned both the history of the food we were making and general cooking tips. He is friendly and easy-going and incredibly easy to talk to. The environment was very comfortable and fun, and the food was delicious! I highly recommend this class - I will always remember this day fondly!

review_text: I took 3 tours with Gray Line while in Santiago. The first one, the Classic Tour, was just ok. They picked me up from my hotel and were caught in traffic so they were 30 min late. We sat in traffic going back towards downtown, picked up another group of people and drove around the downtown area as the guide pointed things out. We worked our way up a hill and then walked up the rest of it for a beautiful view of the city. We then drove back down town to walk around and see some of the sights. For me, it was too much time in the car and not enough time 'out' seeing the sights. There isn't too much to see in downtown, so maybe that was why? We were supposed to be done around 6pm and I got back to my hotel at 830pm due to traffic. This tour was just ok for me. The next day I was picked up right on time for the Valpariso and Coastal del Mar tour. Our driver Walter and guide Carolina were out of this world awesome. We drove about an hour and had a pit stop for a bathroom break and some shopping. Got back on the road and about 30 min later we made it to Valpo. Went to the top of a hill for great views of the city. Took an incline car down, awesome! Had lunch at a very nice and yummy restaurant with great views. Drove to Vina del Mar and stopped for photos along the water. This was the best tour I took while in Chile. Our driver kept us safe, drove well (seems odd I mention this but I have had some bad drivers) the car was cool and ready when we were. Carolina was amazing. She gave us history and facts, chatted like she was our friend, took photos for us, looked out for us and was just marvelous. My third tour was relaxing. Carolina's husband was actually my driver and guide and he was just as sweet as she was. I was the only one on this tour so I was picked up promptly and on time. The drive to Concha was easy with minimal traffic. He pointed out things along the way and once at the winery offered to take photos, got my ticket and walked me in. I took a tour from a winery guide around the grounds and the vineyards, including samples of 3 wines and a souvenir wine glass. Did a little shopping and once done met back up with my guide and back to Santiago we went. The van on each of these tours was clean (inside and out) the drivers were great as well as the guides.

review_text: If you are planning on doing any activities in Futaleufu go with Bochinche, I can guarantee that it will make your entire visit to Futaleufu better! We did rafting and fishing with them and both were fantastic experiences. Giorgia helped us figure out what activities to do to maximize our time in Futaleufu and beyond the rafting and fishing she gave us wonderful tips on where to eat, where to stay, and travel logistics- she is simply the best! I am not exaggerating when I say we looked into changing our flights back to the US just to have a couple more days to do additional activities with Bochinche, they are fantastic! Rafting- due to water conditions we did the Rio Azul and a portion of the Futaleufu. The Rio Azul canyon is so beautiful and the rafting is super fun and exciting, the Futaleufu is like nothing I have ever experienced- the energy and power of the river is a once-in-a-lifetime experience and it is wildly beautiful. I was a little (maybe a lot) nervous before we went, but our guides Nico and Daniel were fantastic, super capable, extremely knowledgeable, and great at what they do. They are very professional and very focused on safety, but still, ensure that it is a ton of fun and you have a great time. As others have mentioned the gear is top-notch, and there are multiple safety boats with every trip, and most importantly the people are the best. It is an amazing experience top to bottom. Afterward, they host a little picnic which is a ton of fun and lets you enjoy the post-adrenaline rush! On the way back to town you have the option to buy photos, don't sleep on these- Jasmine is a super talented photographer and really captures the energy and excitement of the rafting but also takes lovely photos of people. The photos are a very reasonable extra charge that is worth every penny. The next day we went fly fishing on a calmer part of the river with Fly Jorge, it was so beautiful and my husband caught a ton of fish- it was a great day and Bochinche organized it so that everything was easy and smooth. Finally, they sell really pretty jewelry made by a local artist in the office, I got two pairs of fantastic silver earrings that I've worn almost every day since and always get compliments on them. Everyone at Bochinche is fantastic, it was a true pleasure to spend time with all of them and I am confident that you will have an amazing experience with them as they are excellent at what they do and go above and beyond for their guests. Review of: Rafting Azul a Macal - Futaleufu River

review_text: Great half day in the Andes! I must admit it isn't for beginners, and is not an instructor led trip. The details given on trip advisor/viator are accurate, but some reviews made it seem like you had an instructor with you and that's not the case. The hotel pick up and drop off was timely and professional, and they provided everything needed in order to successfully mountain bike. It is a mountain bike park, and I did fall a couple of times being a beginner. It was a beautiful view though and a nice way to escape the city for a half day. Highly recommend this travel company for moderate to experienced mountain bikers! Thanks for your review! We are glad you had a nice experience! This trip is auto guided. The park has very well signage and rescue service so we think guiding is not necessary but you can ask for it as an extra. We give premium electric double suspension mountain bikes with protection accessories (helmet, knee pads and gloves) plus private transportation to the park with a person who set the bike for you. Also we include the park fee and a snack. I personaly think its not accurate to say its not for beginners. The bike park has different level pistes as. ski resort. Of course as in a ski resort if you are a beginner you can fall and if you go for the next level piste it could be dangerous but it doesn't mean the ski resort or the activity is not for beginners. We don't recommend this trip if you don't practice this sport at home. But there are trail for beginners. The difficulty increase in summer because the loose gravel. We hope to see you soon in new trips with us! Matías

review_text: After a lot of research on what we wanted to do and see during our visit to Santiago we determined we had to find a tour operator that could meet our high expectations. Chile Off Track provided a city tour & food tasting and wineries tours that lived up to those expectations. The first day we met our guide Suzie for a day of learning about Santiago's history while sampling numerous food options along the way. As she got to know us she tailored the tour even more to our needs which we greatly appreciated. She spent more time than she had to ensuring we were enjoying ourselves. The second day we ventured out to two wineries for tours and tasting. They were Concha y Toro & Santa Rita each were very good with 3 tastings each. While at Santa Rita we had lunch at their restaurant which I highly recommend. It was a very memorable two days and were not disappointed at all. Something to remember and this is why you hire a tour operator like Chile Off Track is they handle everything you just show up which we appreciated. In Chile as well as in Argentina you have to have reservations to visit any of the wineries and they offer few tours in English. Let them do the planning for you. We recommend Chile Off Track while visiting Chile HI! We are happy to hear that you had 2 great tours with us and that you liked our guide Suzie! I hope you will keep us in mind for our next visit to Chile! Warm regards, Suzanne.

review_text: I was unsure about taking my children on this 3 day tour as i had heard some mixed reviews about the trip from other travellers who had used other companies. I was so impressed by the level of professionalism and service from the minute we were picked up until we were dropped off in Uyuni. We opted to pay for an extra seat so that we could have the trip to ourselves. We had plently of room and were comfortable the entire trip. Our driver was extremely friendly and helpful. The accomodation on the 1st day was simple but clean and the salt hotel on the 2nd night was amazing!!! All our meals were supplied and the food was delicious. We were abit concerned that we would be hungry along the way but there was so much food at each meal that we were full until the next meal. The scenery along the way was absolutely breathtaking and was so different to anything i have ever seen. The different coloured lagoons, the geysers,the hot springs, rock climbing and of course Salar de Uyuni. It was an epic adventure that my whole family enjoyed. We travelled with 3 children aged 6, 10 & 12 and they enjoyed it just as much as we did. Many thanks to Jorge from Cota6000 who organised the tour. He also gave us plenty of tips and advice on Atacama and we also stayed in his Air bnb which was also great. Great location near the bus terminal and Atacama Centro. Thank you for the confidence!!

review_text: We are very seasoned travelers but even so this would be our first visit to Valparaiso. Where to start? Who to contact? Who do we trust with this all to short visit? I checked out Ruta Valparaiso's website and was taken with Leo and the tours and guide options he offers. Booking online was so easy. A few emails and we were ready to go on a full day walking tour. At this distance there is always a worry, will anyone actually show up for us? It happened to us in China and Kenya. But we had no need to worry at all. We were greeted at the cruise port at 8 a.m. by a smiling Christián Cangas, a native from Valparaiso. Even better since our Spanish is rough at best- he lived in the U.S. from the ages of seven to 14 and speaks English fluently and without accent. We could not have been made to feel more welcome-the sign he was holding left little doubt who was there for us. We could not have been made to feel more welcome- more like dear old friends than tourists there to be dragged around. I was so relieved he was there I gave hi a huge hug- he took it in stride I was in ankle braces due to an injury and Cristian had just had knee surgery but that didn't slow us down one bit. We walked, we bused, we took the ascensors, we meet artist Mario Celedon hard at work on a mural. We visited an open air market, got into the back non touristy areas. in one day we saw Valpo from the harbor to the hills. We had a request for a late lunch of non-tourist native Chilean cuisine. Christián settled on Jaibay Cordero a small wonderful cafe. My husband had Pastel de Choclo, a shepherd’s pie with cornmeal. I had Centolla Filo, king crab in a filo dough. We also shared a side dish of papas merken, potatoes flavored with the spice that Gail had bought in the market. It was so good we've tried to replicate it but it must be the Valpo setting- ours just wasn't as good. Valparaiso reminds us of many familiar cities. Like San Francisco, it is comprised of several neighborhood hills (the peaks are 300 meters above sea level) covered with houses. Like Burano, the houses are brightly colored a real treat for the eyes. Like Venice, the city is full of winding streets that no map can adequately cover, causing even natives to get lost if they go down the wrong street. Like Paris, it is very bohemian. Valparaiso loves its art, and there are outdoor murals everywhere you look. We fell in love with Valpo and adopted Cristian. Before we went I thought this might be a one off trip but I miss Valpo so much I can't wait until I have the chance to return. We've stayed in touch with Ruta Valparaiso via Cristian- we feel we have a friend in this wonderful city. Cristian and Ruta Valparaiso gave us the feeling of warm welcome, friendliness and opened our eyes to this most magnificent city. Valpo has heart and soul and Ruta Valparaiso lets you see both perfectly.. For a full story we have blog post http://worldtrippers.com/12soam/12c_cruise2/l120303.htm Wow, I´m speechless with your comment! You definitely have a friend here in Valpo. I too am very happy to have stayed in contact with you. Thanks to this activity, I get the chance to meet wonderful people like you from far away places! I can feel that we made a great connection and that you also were able to connect in deeper terms with this historic, magical and unique port. I´m so glad that you were able to and still see you following up on it. This city has a heart and soul as you say and you´re in it! Big hugs, and keep in touch! Cristián

Since we were leaving that evening, we also worked it out to make the length of the tour just right so that we could bring our luggage and end it at the airport. Ignacio was a fun tour guide, very informative on the history of the area and Chile, and it was nice to be able to get a feel for the place from a local. I would use City Trekking again when I visit Chile again. Dear Andrew Glasser, How are you? Thank you for having chosen us! Having met you and your wife has been very especial! It feels very outdated - little thought has been given to the environments the animals are in nor their ability to socialise and thrive. I'm sure they are sufficiently looked after but the conditions are apparent the second you walk in - two African elephants kept in a tiny concrete enclosure that in no way even tries to recreate their natural terrain. Generally, most animals seem cramped and in unexciting exhibits. I've been to some wonderful zoos in other countries that seem to truly go above and beyond in caring for their animals and highlighting the conservation role of the institution but this one feels like a very sad, very outdated tourist trap.

There are some binoculars with no further charge. The cost for entrance is very reasonable to my justice. About 7 dollars during the week and twice the price during weekend and holidays. I strongly recommend to go there as of the first trip in Santiago, as you can have an espacial idea of where to go and visit.

review_text: My wife and I were in Santiago after a cruise and planned on staying 2 days before flying back home. We met our tour guide at our hotel, Folke, who immediately made us feel at ease and was the most charming gentleman one could imagine. He is a native born Chilean of Scandinavian parents, who spoke English with a beautiful European accent, and who also spoke fluent Spanish, and several other languages. We took a full day tour, which was customized to our desires, along with the usual tourist sites. We had a private driver both days. We were able to book the next day as well at the last minute, which was a wine tour at Santa Rita winery, with an airport transfer after that. The winery was more than we expected and was a fine finish to a wonderful trip. We stopped for lunch at a nice restaurant in Barrio Italia. One of the nice things about Folke was that he was flexible as we went along, and if we wanted to "detour", he was totally fine with it. We had a great walking tour of the center of Santiago, very leisurely and quite informative. We really got to know and appreciate what a beautiful city Santiago is and from Folke's prospective, it seemed even nicer. You could tell Folke was proud of his city and country. We would definitely recommend this tour group and especially Folke. A very interesting man, to say the least. He genuinely enjoys what he is doing and it shows.

The best part is you dont even have to be staying at the hostel to book with them.... trust me on this, book all your excursions through them.

review_text: My husband and I were sleep deprived and cranky after travelling almost 24 hours to get to San Pedro de Atacama. But Jorge turned around our mood and energy with his fantastic tour of the skies near SPdA. At Jorge's suggestion, we did the SAT 2 tour on March 3 to avoid the brightness of the waxing moon. We were the only ones on the tour that night. Jorge picked us up at 11:30 p.m. from our hotel outside of SPdA, and drove approximately 15 minutes to his property for the tour. He had set up comfortable camping-type chairs with blankets and a heater, which made the cold night very comfortable. The tour started with Jorge giving us a fascinating lesson on astronomy. As part of his lesson, we looked at different parts of the clear skies, which were getting darker and even more beautiful as the moon set. Jorge really makes various historical figures and astronomical concepts come to life - my husband and I couldn't help but stay awake and engaged despite our tiredness! After Jorge's lesson, we had an extended food break that was basically a second dinner. We drank the much-celebrated delicious asparagus soup that lives up to the hype, yummy! Jorge and his assistant also put out a huge spread of other snacks and beverages: brownies, hot chocolate, tortilla chips, guacamole, fresh fruit on skewers, wine, coffee, chocolate, etc. After our bellies were full and the moon had set, we spent another hour or so looking at the skies through Jorge's telescopes. He pointed out many difficult objects that looked like nothing more than smudges or empty space, but through the telescopes a whole new world was opened up to us, consisting of nebulae, stars, galaxies and planets. Jorge's passion for stargazing is evident. He excitedly kept pointing out different objects in the sky, and was patient and friendly in answering all questions. Thanks to Jorge, I will never look at the night sky in the same way! The tour ended at around 4 a.m., with Jorge taking photos of me and my husband against the backdrop of the Milky Way. What a great way to commemorate the tour! He also took a photo of the sky without us. Jorge emailed me the photographs the next day; I have attached one of them to this review so you can see what is in store for you! This tour is more expensive than other stargazing tours in SPdA, but it is well worth it. You will learn a lot, see a lot through a variety of telescopes (so you see a LOT of detail!), and will get some amazing photographs from Jorge that will ensure lasting memories. Also, Jorge cares about your experience, which is why he times the tours so that you avoid the brightness of a waning or full moon, and refuses to schedule tours when the moon is too bright. He will also reschedule tours when the skies are cloudy. I heartily recommend Jorge and his tour!

review_text: We took this tour in November. We had requested Vanessa for our guide, but got her brother Gabriel, instead. He was driver and guide. He picked us up punctually at 7am. By 7:30, he had picked up 2 more couples, making us 7 in the van. 2 in the back seat, 3 in the middle seat, and one up front with Gabriel. So unfortunately, one couple was split up during the long drive. We began our drive out of Santiago. Gabriel talked the whole way, about his family, the house he built, how he and his wife have their own business separate from Stamps, how his siblings moved away and one moved back, etc. At 9:30 we stopped at a small cafe where Gabriel said we could use the toilet. 300 pesos each. It was clean. At 10:15 he stopped at some old army barracks. Not much to see there. A short while later we arrived at the reservoir. We stopped for some photos then went deeper into the valley and more reservoir. It was lovely with some snow capped mountains in the distance. Gabriel asked us to go exploring around the area a bit while he set up a table and chairs with 7 tuna sandwiches, chips, strawberries, cookies and wine. The sandwiches were very good and the strawberries huge and sweet. There is not much to explore, and it is rocky. Not boulder rocky, but small irregular rocks making it difficult to walk. Nothing to explore, really. After about 5-10 minutes the 6 of us just kind of stood around waiting. It was breezy and the wind was cold! Luckily Gabriel set the table up along the van to help block the wind and we were comfortable. For the next 2+ hours we sat there looking at the view and snacking. We tried to get to know the other 2 couples better, but Gabriel has a tendency to take over the conversations. He is nice enough, but he likes to hear his own views, and he has a view on many things. The other 2 couples were very nice and when we were able to talk with them it was very enjoyable. At 1:30 we packed up and headed back. We stopped at a waterfall on the way out. It was the best part of the trip. It was a small waterfall, with a very short "hike" to get to it. We were all happy to take photos. We stopped again at the cafe to use the toilet. 300 pesos. The ride back was another couple hours and Gabriel talked 75% of the time to the passenger in the front seat. The fellow knew Gabriel's dad. We were the last to be dropped off, being the first picked up. We got back to our hotel after 4pm. We had arrived in Santiago via cruise ship, and had taken full day tours in several of the ports. This tour was the most expensive, and the only one that disappointed us. We did not realize that 5 hours would be spent driving, and 2 hours just sitting around looking at the water. It was pretty, but in hindsight, we would rather have saved the $220 usd and spent the day in the city. If you are happy to sit and look at a view, this might be for you. If the guide could have added value that would have helped. Hope this helps you. Have a great trip! Santiago has some beautiful parks.

review_text: This was an excellent introduction to the main sites in the Torres del Paine and the Cueva del Mirodor. Nicolas was an informative and engaging guide (bilingual- Spanish/English) and Roberto a great, safe driver. The tour is by a comfortable minibus. It seats about 12. We were picked up outside our Puerto Natales AirBnB a little after 7am and returned about 5pm. REMEMBER- you must separately purchase your national park entry tickets online for both the park and the cave. They are not included in the tour price. Download the tickets to your phone when purchased as there is no reception in the park. We brought our own food but there are stops where drinks and food can be bought. There are also a couple of stops with toilet facilities. We stopped plenty of times to observe and photograph wildlife as well as at the planned viewing stops on the itinerary. We would highly recommend this tour.

review_text: I was looking for party and in nice company yesterday. We decided to go for "La Feria", because we as non-locals were told that it is a place to go in Santiago if you are looking for techno. So far, so good. We queued a little to get in but we were moving fast and the line was more for keeping the tension alive, as the club was not quite full when we finally hit the dancefloor, but as techno-lovers we came and we did not care mucho. We took some Piscocolas and beers, consumed in the club, paid everything - needless to mention. We danced, we made out - long story short: we had a good time. For two hours. After those two hours a security guy suddenly came up to us, grabbed me and threw us out of the club. The explanation was: Falta respeto. Which I did not understand contextually, because as described above we were having a party, we did not do anything illegal or molested others, we simply enjoyed ourselves. At the door I tried to argue, as my Spanish serves for everyday use. But they constantly kept repeating: Falta respeto, which I still do not understand what they were actually trying to tell me. The lady at the entrance even involved the police. The friendly officers of course could not do anything for nobody in the situation and wished us a very good night after a little small talk. I keep thinking the situation over and over but still cannot find a plausible answer why it happened. But I have two theories: First, we got kicked out of the club for paying entrance, consuming drinks, dancing and making out. Which is exactly what a club is for, I thought. But maybe I am mistaken, and you go to techno clubs for having very decent conversations. I let you decide. Or second, they kicked us out because of my racial profile, for being whiter and taller than most of the people here. Which sounds weird for me, but racism unfortunately exists in all societies and people are misguided so many times. Again, the decision is yours. Anyhow: This club does not treat its customers respectfully. Something like this never happened to me before and I am still puzzled and shocked at the same time. This is not the experience I am looking for and I cannot recommend spending even a single Peso on the service they pretend to provide. Neither to even to even talk about “La Feria” as a club, as you are not allowed to dance and kiss on the non-dancefloor.

review_text: If exploring the town you will no doubt come across this impressive cathedral, which dates from the late 1880’s. Near the shores of the picturesque Strait of Magellan it's Chile’s southern most diocese of the Catholic faith. Its exterior has a lovely buttery cream colour, a reddish roof with a single bell tower and clock face.The building appears longer and narrower without the usual pronounced cruciform structure. Apart from a brilliantly coloured Christ in the cupola and the single rows of columns, the interior adornment is rather plain but still very charming. We visited late in the afternoon as the hours are split - Monday to Friday 09.00 - 12.00 and then 15.00 - 20.00, until 13.00 Saturday and Sunday mainly for services. Make time to visit as it sits in a commanding position in the main square area - Plaza Muñoz Gamero – don’t be put off by the surrounding fence. Enjoy your experience!
