review_text: I just completed a 7 day 6 night ski/snowboard week as arranged by Santiago Aventures. We chose to book a self-guided tour because we wanted a complete skiing/snowboarding experience and read many places that roads can be difficult to drive on. They arranged the week for us and here are the good and bad points. Pros: -They affiliate with Powderlodge in Farrellones and they are an awesome, boutique hotel that is just like being in your ski house but with better cooks -Their driver Chris was great. He was always on time and he gave us lots of interesting information on Chile. He spoke impeccable English. -They provide you with most of the week planned out for you which is what I wanted because I wasn't planning the trip on a whim, (the week before we hiked the Inca Trail to Machu Picchu which had to be booked 6 months in advance) -They readily answer emails and will help figure out an itinerary that works for what you want. Cons: -they do not arrange for a way to get to Valle Nevado from Powderlodge, but Christian (hotel owner) can help you with that. This is a con because my contact agent at Santiago Adventures previously informed me that we could walk to each mountain base and so my husband and I didn't take cash out at the airport. Then, at the mountains, their ATMs didn't have cash either so we almost didn't have a way to get to Valle until Christian helped sort this out. -they should stay more up to date in regards to conditions when their clients are there for the week. We were at El Colorado, Valle Nevado and La Parva where the snow was great. Then, when we went to Portillo and Arpa, the snow was awful. I would have liked to have been told of the poorer snow conditions and given an option to do something else like mountain biking, four-wheel driving, snowmobiling, winery tours, etc. In retrospect, I can say I would have gone to Portillo for the history experience but was bored there after just one day. And Arpa, backcountry skiing that had snow worse than what I experience on the east coast, I would have loved to have been given a choice to do something else had someone offered. They should stay up to date on conditions and offer alternatives as I was bored my second day at Portillo and hated the snow that I rode at Arpa. (I am a snowboarder so maybe skiers liked the icy conditions better but being a season pass holder at Killington for 7 years and knowing how to ride ice, I can say that I actually disliked the conditions at Arpa more.) -My itinerary said that there would be a lunch box for the day we went to Arpa and there wasn't. So my husband and I were in the back country with no food or water all day. We would have brought something had we known but like I said, my itinerary said it would be provided. In conclusion, I would recommend Santiago Adventures if you want your ski trip in Chile planned out for you. They were a good company and offer a good service. My recommendation is that they think a little more in regards to the clients so that a snowboarder like myself, doesn't get stuck at places like Portillo (where it's definitely catered towards skiers-t-bars everywhere) and icy backcountry snow at Arpa. This means that if I hadn't used Santiago Adventures, I would not have done a 2nd day at Portillo and would have checked into how Arpa's snow conditions looked before booking so that I could have done other activities that Chile has to offer.

review_text: We stayed in San Pedro for 6 days and one of the things on our list was El Tatio Geysers. We had our own transport so we were going to self drive. All the advice was to leave by 430am so that you could see the geysers at their best because is coldest at dawn and this means the steam is at highest view volume. However none of us felt like getting up that early and driving in the dark on what we heard was a bad road which would have lots of tourist buses and mini vans on it .... So we left at midday instead and also decided to go via Puritama hot springs which looked like a viable alternative route to el tatio from San Pedro. There was no traffic but the dirt road to Puritama was very bad, rutted, steep uphill, and many stretches of more than 1km where there was only room for 1 vehicle. To top it off there was a precipitous drop on one side. Luckily there was no traffic because I would not have enjoyed reversing down that windy track (downhill vehicles have right of way). After a slow hour we made to to Puritama where no one felt like bathing so we continued on the terrible road towards El Tatio. Wonderful scenery and only saw one other vehicle in 3 hours which is how long it ended up taking. We had a 4wd which was really needed. By the time we got to El Tatio all the crowds had left and we had the place completely to ourselves. While not quite as spectacular as some of the photos it was still really engrossing to wander around observing the many big and some very small geysers and bubbling mud holes (stick to the marked paths !) and being there all by ourselves. review_text: The 7 day Torres del Paine W trek starts and finishes at EcoCamp, which is a great experience in itself. It doesn't matter if you are in a Standard dome or a luxurious Suite dome, it's the EcoCamp vibe that leaves a lasting memory. The community domes where groups gather to meet, eat, relax and socialize is the heart of EcoCamp and is where I spent the most time when not on the trail. The food was awesome! The staff were always friendly and helpful. My guides Danny and Paz did a great job keeping us safe on the trail and their knowledge of the geography, plants and wildlife was exceptional. The walking was well paced and not overly demanding although the weather conditions did prevent my group from ascending to the two highest points in the W. The four seasons in one-hour weather is also what keeps this trek interesting. The wind gusts constantly remind you how nature rules in the wilderness. The Torres del Paine W trek should definitely be on your bucket list and Cascada Expediciones offers the perfect way to achieve your goal. review_text: We’ve taken winery tours all around the world, but never seen one like Lapostolle Clos Apalta Winery, outside of Santa Cruz, Chile. This boutique winery was set up by the grand-daughter of the creator of Grand Marnier liquor – Louis Alexandre Marnier Lapostolle. It clearly has been a labor of love for her and she was able to provide strong financial support to the building of this winery. The winery is located on a rural road off of the main highway to Santa Cruz and shares the road with three other very reputable wineries. The tours are limited to eight or less people (we had four) booked in advance by reservation and are available at least in either English or Spanish. Our English tour guide was a former English teacher and was an excellent guide. The winery is about eight floors high, built into rock hillside, so that the wine making process can rely on gravity as much as possible and avoid pumps. The “roof” level is a garden. The tour starts one level below the roof where the grapes that had been hand picked are received and a team of women individually remove the grapes from the stems. The grapes are then taken and lowered by gravity into the primary fermenters, which are oak (unusual in this day of stainless steel primary fermenters). After primary fermentation, the wine is gravity few to the oak casks in the level below. After a year, the casks are taken by elevator to a level below for blending and storage on oak for another couple of years. Finally the aged wine is lowered to the last level for bottling. One of the highlights of the tour is the visit to the “two year aging room” which has a huge glass topped table in the middle to serve as a bar for tasting the wines. While there, the tour guide turns on the lighting under the glass table where you can see the stairs that go down under the glass table (one end cantilevers up to allow the owner to descend the stairwell). The first floor under the table is a “library” of wine bottles that have been given to the owner from other wineries. The second level below the table is another library of wine racks that hold 250 bottles of each vintage that has been produced at the winery. The wines include a 2005 that won the Wine Spectator best red wine in its Top 100 Wine ranking. The only “negative” is that the price of the tour is US$40 per person which sounds very expensive when one compares it to other wineries but given that it is a very restricted tour with a quality guide and you get to try some of the best wines in the world (costing over US$100 per bottle), the admission fee is appropriate.

review_text: If you haven't seen penguins, go! The fishing boats (5000 pesos each) out to the islands go at random times, but sit and have a drink, and you might get on one. Minimum 10 people. We stayed in a cabana, 50m from the seashore. Could hear the waves all night and there was a lovely patio to sit out on. The birdlife all along the beach was superb. campingpandeazucar@hotmail.com or granatacama@gmail.com to book a cabana. We spent weeks trying to find these! The cabanas were basically equipped (no kitchen knife in the one we had and only one wine glass) but were beautiful with the bedroom overlooking the Pacific and a lovely ensuite bathroom. Electricity is from a single solar panel and you can't plug anything extra in. Bring matches, a penknife (with a tin and bottle opener) and a torch. The bed linen was very luxurious. Don't expect hot water all the time or a state of the art shower - you are in the middle of nowhere! If you are bus/taxiing in, bring all your food with you and don't expect to buy anything in the Park. The restaurants in the fishing village are good and very reasonable but if you want breakfast and to do your own thing, bring it with you! A car would have been useful, but as we were only there for 3 nights, we could do all the local walks. We were handed a tsunami leaflet on arrival and this was somewhat unnerving. Chanaral is heavily polluted and we are glad we didn't stop there for long.

review_text: This museum is interesting and thought provoking, well worth the challenges of the layout and systems. It is right by the Quinta Normal metro stop. They ask you for ID when you enter (at least when you get an audio guide). If you don't have anything they recognise (they didn't like my UK passport) you have to fill in a form with your name and address. If you are not a Spanish speaker you will need to have an audio guide at a cost of 20,000 pesos. The layout doesn't seem to follow an obvious route and some of the signs are incorrect. For example, all the signs for the cafe direct you to the third floor. The floor plan of the third floor shows you where the cafe is. Interestingly, the cafe is on the ground floor, outside the main entrance and round the back. It serves cheap refreshments, so worth a visit. The displays themselves are excellent and you learn a lot about the Pinochet era. Moving and thought provoking. Highly recommended.

review_text: We booked two tours online with Chilean Wine Lovers: the first, a tour of three Maipo Valley wineries, the second, a tour of the Emiliana winery on our way to Valparaiso and Vina del Mar. Mauricio was quick to reply and confirm dates, but we had difficulty paying on his site (we found out later that this part of the site was indeed not working), and we were concerned once we arrived that because the payment hadn't worked, there would be no tour. Our followup email to Mauricio, asking what we should do, did not receive a reply, so we were a bit anxious when we reached Santiago. Turns out, there was nothing to worry about - the tour was still on, Mauricio was very relaxed about the payment and the site was fixed by the time we reached Chile. We were on our own with Pablo for both tours, as Mauricio was studying for his winemaker's exams. Pablo was an exceptional guide, versed in the geography, demography and sociology of his country. He was able to answer our many questions, and seemed to know exactly the type of information that would be of interest us! Our first tour combined a small, family-run organic winery, a tour of the notoriously private Perez Cruz operation (only two tours get in per day, we were one of them), and a tour of the sprawling Santa Rita operation. We loved how each tour was different, and we learned different things from each. On Day 2, we toured the Emiliana organic winery in the Casablanca valley, and visited Valparaiso. We enjoyed our time so much at these two locations that we decided to give Vina del Mar a pass. At Emiliana, we were partnered with a group from Canada (where we are from) for the tour. We had a wonderful time with these folks, only to discover during the tasting that they were our flight crew for our return trip in two days! In Valparaiso, we visited Pablo Neruda's unique house, La Sebastiana, and had a wonderful seafood lunch nearby at Oda Pacifica - where we had the best ceviche ever! From there, we scaled two of Valparaiso's hills and took many photos of the amazing murals. It was a wonderful two days with Pablo and should we have the opportunity to return to this amazing country, we will again book a Chilean Wine Lovers' tour!

review_text: Our party of three travelled to Chile in November 2015 and was looking for a good vineyard tour outside of Santiago. We did some research and found O'Higgins Tours based out of Rancagua. Brian was very prompt with his responses and we quickly had a date and time picked--O'Higgins was very accommodating to our schedule. Also, Brian gave us a heads up about the commuter trains being temporarily out of service, and gave us an excellent recommendation for getting a bus to Rancagua. Mauricio picked us up at the bus station in Rancagua right on time. The car ride to the Anakena vineyard took about 45 minutes or so, during which time Mauricio gave us a great introduction to the region and its history. His English is excellent. The Anakena vineyard is breathtakingly beautiful. Acres of vineyards under a clear blue sky, with the Andes in the background. The tour guide at Anakena was also very informative and took us through the whole process from grape to bottle. The tour was capped off with a tasting at their magnificent bar. Their carmenère (varietal which is Chile's specialty) was fantastic. All of us--we three, Mauricio, and the Anakena tour guide (whose name escapes me)--had a great chat during the tasting. Afterwards, Mauricio drove us back to the bus station to complete the tour. I had the sense that it's a little off the beaten path, but in my experience this is usually where you find the most memorable travel moments. And O'Higgins Tours certainly impressed with their knowledgeable personnel and courteous service. I'd recommend these folks in a heartbeat; if ever I find myself in Chile again, I'd definitely do another of their tours. Thank you to Brian and Mauricio for helping to make our trip to Chile a great one!

review_text: We went to Pucon for 3 days and I would almost have to say that it was the best part of our trip. We did not plan anything ahead of time except for the hostel we were staying at. We arrived late in the afternoon and walked around Pucon to get acquainted. We found a little agency off the main road that would take us to Villarica the next morning. They size you for a snowsuit and climbing gear. We needed to bring sunglasses & sunblock (reflection off the snow), bottled water and lunch (sandwiches). We arrived at the agency around 7:00am and arrived at Villarica around 8:00-8:30 by taxivan. We then took a chairlift up to the starting point which was about 10-15min ride. From there you start to climb zig-zag up the mountain. It's cold and scary because all you have keeping you up on the mountain is your boots (only sometimes with snow-picks) and an ice-pick. We rested a couple of times and reached the crater around 12:00-1:00pm. Along the way there were amazing places to take breathtaking pictures. We actually climbed INTO the crater, kept some volcanic rocks and took pictures of the lava splashing up close to us. The smell is a little nausiating but you put up with it because of the experience. On the way back you slide on your bum down the mountain on man-made snowslides. Your pants and bum get wet but it's lots of fun. We arrived back at the agency around 4:30 and immediately made plans to vist the hot springs "Las Termas". Go to the natural ones at the top of the mountain and you'll melt away all the physical discomfort from the day. You should be in pretty good shape to undertake this activity but if your group is too fast for you, slower groups along the way will always welcome an addition. Make sure you go on a clear day-other people who went with us were making it their 2nd trip because the first time they couldn't see anything. Have fun and enjoy!

If you´re traveling with luggage, while making a reservation ask them to pick you up from the busstop, www.emiliana.cl/contact-us, otherwise it is 10 min. dirt road walk. review_text: Taking this tour with guide Borris and driver Ariel was the perfect introduction to this amazing country. My husband and I got off the plane at 9am, dropped our stuff off at the hotel, and began the tour at 12. The plan was to do anything and everything to stay awake until it was bed time in order to lessen the onset of jet lag. We were in for a real treat and were enthralled with the things we saw on our tour through Santiago. With stops at Santa Lucia Hill, the Bella Vista District, and Santiago's bustling city center, we didn't have time to think about being sleepy. The following day we had another outstanding Servitour experience going to the Andes mountains and its surrounding vibrant communities. Ariel was our driver again (very happy about that...he is phenomenal) but this tour was narrated by Estéban. The descriptions of his experiences hiking and skiing and snowboarding were so interesting to listen to. He is very connected to the earth and I appreciated how he expressed his sacred views of the land. He was knowledgeable and passionate and was an excellent guide! All 3 of our guides spoke English verrrry well. My husband and I appreciated that. Best part of the trip was standing atop a silent mountain and watching the incredible condors gliding in between the Andes’ peaks. Priceless. It is also important to note that I felt safe everywhere I went. Even when I was alone. Take these tours for sure!! Thank you, Ariel, Borris, and Estéban for such great experiences! Dear Mrs, Thank so much for your great comments about your experience with us knowing Santiago. We work everyday to deliver experiences!! We hope to see you again to continue knowing more about Chile and surroundings. Kind regards

review_text: I was leary about going to Torres del Paine in the winter because I could find very little information before I left but I'm so glad I went anyway! I flew into Punta Arenas and rented a car to drive myself there. It took me about 4.5 hours but the roads were great. It's a nicely paved highway from Punta Arenas to Puerto Natales then a great dirt/gravel road starting just outside Puerto Natales. I was alone but it was an easy drive and the scenery gave me a great sense of the place and its stark grandness. I spent about a week at the Hosteria Lago Grey which I loved. The place was perhaps 1/4 occupied so I had a nice room with a great view (room 701). I could lie in bed and see the mountains and look across the lake to the glacier. The staff and food were great. I took the boat across the lake to see Glacier Grey on their first trip of the season (when I first arrived the boat wasn't running yet). Cold but beautiful. I did some hiking around the park (no more than a few hours at a time, no major trekking) which was just amazing. I also drove all over the place and, in winter, there were virtually no other people or cars anywhere. I had the whole place to myself so could go as slow as I wanted, stop in the middle of the road, do whatever. It was fantastic! I was even pleasantly surprised by the weather. It was cold now and then but not nearly as cold as I expected. It was often windy but not always. One day it was blowing at least hurricane strength but with 6 days there I had plenty of gorgous sunny days too. The scenery can't be beat! The mountains are truly amazing while the lower parts of the park are easily accessible (no snow on the ground) and gorgeous in all shades of brown and gold before the spring greenery comes. I saw guanacos galore, condors, hawks, foxes (even a family of 4 foxes who live near the hotel!), skunks and even flamingoes! This was the trip of a lifetime and worth every penny I spent to get there (all the way from Hawaii).

review_text: We've been living in Chile for 3 years and have visited the MIM several times with our young children. Having been to many science centers in Canada and the US, the MIM does not compare - it is small and the quality and variety of exhibits pales in comparison. With that said, as far as Chile goes, the MIM is the only venue of its type and can be a great way to pass a rainy / cold day with young children. Our kids particularly love the bubble room, where they can make giant bubbles of different shapes, in some cases encasing themselves in the bubbles. There are a number of other interactive exhibits that really captivate our kids, like construction sites where they can load and transport dirt, balls that balance on upward airstreams, drawing tables, peg boards where you can make hand / body impressions, etc. Upstairs there are also some good exhibits on electricity and outer space. For very young children (under 4 years, I believe), they have an area where they can colour and play simple computer games. There is also a building block area that is similarly tailored to younger children. In addition to the exhibits, they have a daily schedule of workshops and shows you can sign up for as part of the entrance fee. Unfortunately many of the really interesting ones, like building a robot, are only for older children (over 10 years old)... which really disappointed our 6 and 4 year old boys. Occasionally they have workshops for young children (which my kids never find interesting). They also always have some sort of short movie on a specific topic, like dinosaurs or Chile. The movies are somewhat entertaining, but nothing spectacular or memorable. So, if you are travelling to Santiago with young children and have some time to kill and want to spend it in a kid-tailored venue that is educational, the MIM is a viable option. Personally, we continue to go to the MIM for something to do for 3-4 hours with the kids during the shoulder seasons when the weather is poor and ski season is closed. In good weather there are many other more compelling options (beach, parks, hiking in nature parks, Mampato amusement park, etc.) to entertain the kids.

review_text: A highlight of South America and one of the most wonderful experiences. We did the 3days / 2 nights tour from San Pedro to Uyuni with World White Tours. You travel by land cruiser with stops across the most beautiful landscape, colourful lagunas, Wild Flamingoes, amazing rock formations, wild llamas in lush Greenland, bathe in hot springs and see the most insane amount of mountains peaks and volcanoes. I had no idea how much beauty Bolivia has, the best was saved to last... the Salt Flats. It’s the most surreal experience, stunning landscape where the skies are reflected, and you play with perspective creating incredible memories and pictures. Although you go as a larger group of about 24 (4 cars) with this tour we experienced a lot of the places alone which was amazing... I’ve never experienced being in such a beautiful place with absolute silence! This might be due to our guide Oscar making sure this happened. You meet up with the other cars in certain locations, so you also have the comfort that you are with a larger group that can help each other out. A massive thank you to our guide Oscar! He made us feel welcome, safe and comfortable throughout, it was a pleasure to spend time with him. He made every effort to make it the best tour (which is was). If you can definitely try to request Oscar as your guide, he does Spanish and English tours. In terms of comfort (I like my comfort...), the land cruiser was fine and lots of fun, we played our own music. The food was great, really filling and good mix of veggies, meats and carbs, defo bring snacks though in case you get hungry before lunch. The accommodation on the first night was basic but comfortable and warm, we asked for extra sleeping bags and your so tired from having your mind blown you just pass out! Second night was better with a hot shower! Bring lots of layers it gets cold and hot throughout the day and waterproof boots for the salt plains (or go bare foot). Finally be careful of Altitude sickness, we had a really ill person in our group who had come directly from Santiago, do stay in San Pedro a night to adjust, bring some coca sweets or leaves and then focus on the landscape instead! Enjoy :-)

review_text: We spent a total of 7 days with Maurice and his driver Claudio. We worked with Maurice about a year in advance to develop a custom tour through many of the Chilean wine regions and also to transit through the area. The first day, Maurice and Claudio met us at the Santiago airport to transport us to our lodging in Provedencia. This was at the end of October when Santiago was undergoing protests. Maurice gave us many insights into keeping safe while in the city. Our second day was a foodie tour at the large local market and some select areas to explore. On day three, we explored the Aconcagua Valley and stopped for private tours and tastings at San Esteban/In Situ, Flaherty and Vino El Escorial wineries, with a lunch stop at a local restaurant. Maurice brought wine to pair with the lunch. The fourth day, we head south to the Alto Maipo Valley, We stop at a local place to pick up some unique bread baked in an adobe oven for a snack, then on to Perez Cruz. We have lunch at another local restaurant with a wine pairing of Santa Rita Carmanere. We stop at Maurices house and meet his lovely family over a bottle of wine and finished at Vina Cousino Macul. It is obvious that Maurice has a special relationship with the wineries. Day 5 we head to the Cachapoal and Colchagua Valleys. We spend the morning barrel tasting in the cellars at Alchemy (a must go) and the winemakers prepare lunch for us. We end with a private tour and tasting at Maturana before Claudio drives us to Teno. A week later we reconnect with Maurice to tour the Casablanca Valley. We have tours and tastings at La Recova, lunch and a tasting at Kingston Family wines (they ship to the U.S.) and a final, unscheduled stop at Vina Casa del Bosque before returning us to lodging in Santiago. Our last day, Claudio transports us to the airport. It is obvious that Maurice is highly knowledgable and passionate about wine. He has great relationships with the wineries and we were treated very well everywhere we went. When we were planning our trip we requested boutique to medium size wineries and that was what we got. Our driver Claudio was extremely courteous and professional. If we would return to Chile, we would absolutely book another trip with Maurice.

We have lunch at another local restaurant with a wine pairing of Santa Rita Carmanere. We stop at Maurices house and meet his lovely family over a bottle of wine and finished at Vina Cousino Macul. It is obvious that Maurice has a special relationship with the wineries. Day 5 we head to the Cachapoal and Colchagua Valleys. We spend the morning barrel tasting in the cellars at Alchemy (a must go) and the winemakers prepare lunch for us. We end with a private tour and tasting at Maturana before Claudio drives us to Teno. A week later we reconnect with Maurice to tour the Casablanca Valley. We have tours and tastings at La Recova, lunch and a tasting at Kingston Family wines (they ship to the U.S.) and a final, unscheduled stop at Vina Casa del Bosque before returning us to lodging in Santiago. Our last day, Claudio transports us to the airport. It is obvious that Maurice is highly knowledgable and passionate about wine. He has great relationships with the wineries and we were treated very well everywhere we went. When we were planning our trip we requested boutique to medium size wineries and that was what we got. review_text: I paid for a "tour" for my wife and I to visit the Andes, hoping to stop to take photos and enjoy the scenery along the way. I tried my best to speak the little spanish that I know, but it was only enough to get picked up and dropped off at my hostel. I knew already it was going to be a long day after the bus ride to the MassKi offices. They asked my wife and I to get up at 7:05am for the bus to pick us up. The driver was on time, but for him to come back to the same exact corner to pick up another couple at 8:10am seemed very silly and inefficient. My wife and I could have gotten another hour of sleep and enjoyed the free breakfast at the hostel we were staying in. We started our day at 7am and ended it at 8pm, which was much longer than expected. Since we didn't ski, we were idle for about 10 hours, either waiting at the ski lodge or sitting on the bus, haha, so it felt like a wasted day. There were tons of photo opportunities that I wish we had stopped for. It certainly did not feel like your average "tour." The driver, Mauricio, was really pleasant, and I'm glad that he was able to get us all home safely after a snowy day in the mountains. He's probably the only reason I didn't give this place a 1-star rating.

review_text: As expected, we encountered a bit of rain, but what we were able to see was exceptional. We caught a beautiful sunny day and the 45 min- 1hr walk (pretty flat) each way is not to be missed. It takes you so close and you can see the Italian and French camps at the base.

review_text: We did a 4 day tour from Atacama - Uyuni - Atacama with them last October. We already set our expectations low based on reviews and we actually had a great time. Our driver, Nelson was really great and made us feel comfortable during the whole trip and I think was one of the main reasons we enjoyed, apart from Bolivia being just gorgeous. It was a lot of combined effort by the lovely Bolivia locals, hotel employees, restaurant cooks, and the friendly drivers. The organizers however I think shouldn't be given too much credit. They weren't very helpful and responded late, when we were at their office in Atacama it was hard for them to even give a smile, there was even a guy on the desk who was rude to us, the guy in the Uyuni office wasn't too welcoming either and just left us clueless on what we'll do while waiting for our trip back. I also had an issue with a request I had, requesting them to connect us with the driver. Unfortunately we had a couple of photos taken on our driver's cellphone, he wasn't used to ours so he used his. Obviously I wanted the copies because we didn't have much, so I was patient and had weeks of back and forth emails with promises that they'll have it sent right away. A few months later I follow-up again and they just told me that they could no longer reach him and that he's left the company. How convenient. So really, Bolivia was/is amazing but I won't say it was because of the organizers. I suggest you book somewhere else as there are so many better options. When you get to San Pedro just do a quick walk and you'll find so many companies and you can even haggle for the prices.

review_text: Our whole family (3 children, 2 adults, 2 seniors) recently stayed at the Chile Nativo Riverside Camp and I wanted to write and share how impressed we all were with the location, but even more so the quality of the Chile Nativo staff in dealing with a medical emergency. First off, we loved the Riverside Camp, with great food, wonderful views, a great main dome to eat/relax, and charming canvas tents to stay in (with clean washrooms, heated blankets, power and more). What really impressed us was when my mother had medical issue that became a medical emergency and required treatment. The staff at the camp dropped what they were doing and were all well trained in first aid and helped with the issue. They also quickly alerted local park rangers who dispatched EMT's who came within 10 minutes. We subsequently evacuated to the Puerto Natales hospital, where another Chile Nativo staff member met my mother to act as an interpreter with the local doctors and nurses at the hospital. Our whole family is thankful for the training the team at the camp had, and it prevented a much more serious medical issue. So many thanks to the whole team. Thank you for sharing your experience. We’re glad to hear you enjoyed Riverside Camp and, most importantly, that our team was able to support you during a difficult moment. The safety and well-being of our guests are our top priorities, and we take pride in our staff’s quick and professional response. We’re relieved that your mother received the care she needed and grateful for the efforts of our team, park rangers, and medical staff. We’ll be sure to share your kind words with them. We hope to welcome you again under better circumstances. Wishing you all the best! The Chile Nativo Team

review_text: Arriving in his jeep straight to our hotel door, Guillermo welcomed us with an energetic wave and warm smile, taking us to Chepu to spend our day kayaking and hiking. On the way, we stopped off at a local’s homestead, to collect the kayaks and snacks for the trip ahead, spotting Chile’s famous pudú deer on the way! Kitted and ready to go, we set off – the scenes beheld were breath-taking! The result of a tsunami in the 60s, the trees lining Chepu river stand now as wooden bones emerging from the waters with sunlight beaming through, an ethereal ghost forest. Paddling upstream, we then moored on the bank for a break, we took in the beautiful wildlife including local black cormorants, in the surrounding forests of Chepu. Back on shore, we returned to the homestead, to be greeted with a log fire and traditional cuisine; amazing steak and potatoes, with a great vegetable platter for our vegetarian daughter. Whilst there, we got the opportunity to sample matte tea - a Chepu specialty. Richly infused, matte (mat-té) is herbal and bitter but once stirred with sugar and hot water, sweet and warming – a must-try! Changed out of our wet-gear, we took to the forest for a bushwalk, arriving in its depths by a mini train handmade by the homestead’s residents! With a vast knowledge of the fauna, Guillermo gave us an insightful tour of the forest, and led us down the river; crossing hanging bridges and stepping rocks as the river rushed by made this one eventful energetic trail! By the end, we were all worn out, falling asleep on the drive back to Castro, but couldn’t have asked for a better day, spent with great company. Bilingual, with an inspiring enthusiasm for the great outdoors, we can’t recommend Guillermo highly enough; we’ll definitely be calling on him again for our next adventure! We found Guillermo Retamal through TripAdvisor, on chilespotstourismo.com, then contacting him directly through his email chilespots@gmail.com. Find him also on Instagram @chilespots_travel! review_text: We were booked by our tour company for a visit to see the Balmaceda, Serrano & Tyndall Glaciers & told to report at the quay side at 8.30 prompt. But there are 2 queys, both about 10 mins walk from the hotel, in opposite directions & the hotel did not know which one we should go to. After a slight panic a kind hotel worker discovered that we should really go to a house in the middle of a field! ( just so you know if you do this trip) There we were equipped with excellent spacesuit - like waterproofs which kept us warm & dry for our trip in the zodiac. My husband loved the whole experience, I was less enthusiastic as it started to rain heavily as soon as we set out & didn't stop till we got to the Serrano Glacier an hour later. On a dry day it would be a lovely journey. At the glacier there was a choice of an hours round trip to the base of the glacier on fairly rough terrain or a short easy walk to a view point looking over the water. I opted for the easy option, which was beautiful, & then sat in a comfortable boat till the others came back. There are welcome toilets at the stop. On the return journey we saw sea lions swimming by the zodiac , barking loudly, & Tyndall Glacier at a distance. Our helms man was skilled - we felt safe & well looked after. On return we were given an included lunch, which we hasn't expected, served with great care - delicious! The whole trip took 5 hours, not including getting dressed up in our suits . Good value & enjoyable.

review_text: Cajon del Maipo Embalse el Yeso was our first of two day tours booked with Stamps. IT WAS AMAZING!!! We received everything listed as included in the tour description, but what we didn’t necessarily expect to have included was our awesome tour guide Vanessa. She was so friendly, very knowledgeable about not only our excursion but also Santiago and Chile in general, and was just all around a very cool person. Cajon del Maipo was about an hour and a half drive from our hotel. Along the way we stopped at various sites to get pictures of the beautiful mountain scenery, during which Vanessa explained the significance of certain historical events in the region and answered any questions we asked. The drive to the top is not for the faint hearted, but she was a great driver and the tour company knew what kind of vehicle would be the best and smoothest ride. We passed several buses from other companies whose drivers and tourists looked a little uncomfortable trying to make it up the road. Upon arrival at Cajon del Maipo, we explored the breathtaking scenery and took incredible pictures, while Vanessa set up a full meal on a table and chairs in a spot overlooking the lake and mountains/glaciers. After our short hike to explore the area, we sat down to eat, drink wine, and enjoy good conversation. It was almost surreal to be in such an amazing place enjoying a simple but awesome meal. I’m definitely replicating the sandwiches with hearts of palm added when I get back to the states, so yummy! Everything was absolutely perfect from start to finish on this excursion, probably the most beautiful place I have ever seen, and our tour guide only made the day more wonderful. We ended the day thinking there was no way it could get any better. If you visit Cajon del Maipo and do not book through Stamps Tours, you’re definitely missing out!

review_text: My partner and I have climbed Volcan Villarrica about 5 times between the two of us and with 3 different companies, and this was by far the best experience we have had. We regularly visit the area with large groups of exchange students so we are always on the look out for the best guiding service for our groups, and we had heard good things about Summit Chile so we decided to give them a try when our usual tour company didn't have enough spots for all of our students. The guide to climber ratio was great--10 climbers with 4 guides, and not only that, but all of the guides were clearly very experienced, conscious of all safety precautions, and loved what they were doing (and I cannot say that about the other tour companies). We appreciated the fact that one guide led, another followed behind, and two guides constantly monitored the progess of the group by walking alongside climbers and offering suggestions and monitoring the group pace. All of the guides shared the philosophy that the experience should be fun, safe, and not leave you completely exhausted at the end of the day, whereas some other companies tend to take pride in arriving first at the top of the mountain or doing the climb in the shortest time possible. All other aspects were great--coordinating the visit, the high-quality equipment, transportation to and from our cabins at no extra cost, and even a free trip up the rock wall outside. Highly recommend Summit Chile; we will work with them again on any future group visits to Pucon.

review_text: Torres del Paine National Park is found between the Andes Mountain range and the Patagonian Steppe in the Chilean side of Patagonia. It covers an area of just over 1800 sq km (700 sq mi). The National Park holds within its boundaries a number of glaciers, lakes, rivers and valleys, as well as the famed centerpiece, Cordillera del Paine, where we found the two most recognized rock formations known as Las Torres (the three towering rock formations that give the park its name) and Cuernos del Paine (the Paine Horns). The park is located about 112 km (70 mi) north of the town of Puerto Natales and approximately 312 km (194 mi) north of the city of Punta Arenas. Commercial flights in Chile only fly into the city of Punta Arenas, where you must then take a bus or transfer to the town of Puerto Natales, before continuing to Torres del Paine. Transfers from Punta Arenas to Puerto Natales takes anywhere between 2 1/2 to 3 hours, and then it is another 1 1/2 to 2 hours to get to Torres del Paine National Park. For the longest time, visiting Torres del Paine National Park was reserved for backpackers and hikers willing to 'rough-it'. Accommodations across the National Park were very basic and in order to really see the best sites of the Park you had to spend several nights in tents and refuges around the main trails and circuits. However, as of the last 8 years, this has really changed. New hotels, lodges and very comfortable camping sites have been built all around the Park, allowing almost anyone the chance to see one of the most beautiful National Parks in the World. I read that over 4 million people from all over the world voted on a recognized travel website and named Torres del Paine as the 8th Wonder of the World! Which I would easily vote the same! Today you can visit Torres del Paine in 2 ways: The first is by staying in hotels around around the Park and venturing out on daily excursions to the most famous visitor sites, and the second is by doing the entire W or the O Trekking Circuits around the Paine massif. The entire Park contained clearly marked paths and many refuges and camping sites which provided basic services and shelter for backpackers. These circuits took us anywhere between 6 to 12 days to complete, depending on the pace and the activities you wish to do along the way. How you choose to see Torres del Paine National Park really depends on your budget, your physical condition and on how you wish to experience the Park. Activities offered around the Park range from walks and hikes, to horseback riding, to kayaking, to fly fishing, to navigations across lakes and more. You can see and do it all if you give yourself enough time and plan properly like we did! The views in the park are absolutely breathtaking and I would recommend this to anyone who really appreciates nature in its purest form. Visiting Torres del Paine is recommended during the months of October thru April. During these months the weather is nicer, and daylight hours are long, due to the extreme southern latitude. During the Patagonian Winter (May – August) many trails close and the weather can get too cold for trekking.

review_text: Our 4 full day Antarctica cruise with AntarcticaXXI was completely CANCELLED due to weather. Be very careful with this company and review your contract of carriage with AntarcticaXXI. Upon our arrival in Puntas Arenas, our entire cruise to Antarctica was CANCELLED due to weather. AntarcticaXXI will keep 40% of your entire ticket price to defray their company costs. For instance, a double cabin that cost $30,000 means AntarcticaXXI will keep $12,000 in their pocket for the CANCELLED trip. They will claim you agreed to their Contingency Plan Program for delayed flights to Antarctica. What is not clear is that if AntarcticaXXI CANCELS your trip they will keep 40% of your paid ticket. Francesco Contini, EVP Sales & Marketing, will Fed Ex you an apology letter telling you he is sorry your trip did not operate. What is missing in the apology letter is my check for $12,000 completing my full refund for services not rendered. (Trip cost $30,000) Personally, this is just bad business. Based on AntarcticaXXI's inability to do the right thing by refunding our full ticket prices I can not in good conscience recommend anybody to do business with this company. Francesco... is $12,000 worth a 1 star rating on TripAdvisor to you? Apparently, the answer is YES!!! Between January 28 and January 31, 2015 heavy fog did not permit the operation of any flights to King George Island, the gateway for ANTARCTICA XXI's expeditions. As a result, the departure scheduled to fly to Antarctica on January 28, and arranged for a photographic group, lost the opportunity for a visit to Antarctica. Although never before in the company’s 12-year history have weather conditions delayed a flight to the point of preventing participants from reaching Antarctica, the promotional brochure for the expedition outlined a detailed plan in case of delays. This plan was featured in a dedicated and clearly visible section titled “Contingency Plan” (i.e. not in the “fine print”). It followed the “Important Information” section that strongly recommended the purchase of travel insurance. It stated that in case unfavourable weather would delay the operation of the Antarctic flight, participants would wait in Punta Arenas for an opportunity to fly. The services that would be provided were outlined. It continued by stating that “If by the end of Day 7 (24:00 hours local time) ANTARCTICA XXI will not be able to transport passengers to Antarctica, ANTARCTICA XXI will refund to each passenger 60% of the total rate (excluding discounts, if any) paid for the voyage.” The conditions of the Contingency Plan reflected the nature of the expedition and the complexity of the operation. The 64 participants in this unlucky departure received accommodation and airport transfers in Santiago, round-trip flights from Santiago to Punta Arenas, transportation, meals, and accommodation in Punta Arenas. They received a private excursion on a chartered boat on the Strait of Magellan, as well as other organized excursions in Punta Arenas and surroundings. During the entire time seven acclaimed photography instructors who flew to Punta Arenas from the USA, Canada, Australia, and Great Britain accompanied participants. Emergency mobile phones were provided to participants while in Punta Arenas. A team of 3 front-line staff members from ANTARCTICA XXI escorted and coordinated the group, booking meeting rooms and holding briefings, while a back-office team supported them 24/7. In the flight operations department, meteorologists and veteran Antarctic pilots worked tirelessly, monitoring the weather and preparing flight plans, only to be repeatedly frustrated by persistent fog at King George Island. In Antarctica, a logistics team was on standby at King George islands ready to receive the flight, while a fully provisioned ship with 38 officers, crew, chefs, hotel staff, and 12 polar guides waited for the group to arrive. That is the reason the Contingency Plan is structured as it is. While the conditions of the Contingency Plan were clearly presented prior to reservation, ANTARCTICA XXI has gone beyond. Firstly, with no improvement in the weather conditions in sight, on January 31 ANTARCTICA XXI arranged a charter flight from Punta Arenas to Santiago, as well as airport transfers and accommodation in Santiago. This charter flight was not part of the original itinerary nor of the Contingency Plan. It was organized by ANTARCTICA XXI to provide our valued clients the opportunity to return home as soon as possible, without waiting for the scheduled commercial flights on February 4, thereby avoiding further delay and frustration. Secondly, in conjunction with the group organizers we are developing a special offer designed to offer participants in this unlucky departure the chance to join a future expedition at a significant discount. Everyone at ANTARCTICA XXI deeply regrets that the weather conditions did not allow the operation of the Antarctic flight. We feel for the disappointment experienced by participants, as it is our disappointment also. We recognize that the circumstances our company faced were challenging. But we did everything we could and we cannot see how ANTARCTICA XXI can be blamed in any way for what happened. Francesco Contini Executive Vice President, Sales & Marketing

review_text: Although the village is a replica of Parinacota village in the Altiplano, it does give a faithful impression of the lovely architecture - not everyone will be able to travel above 4,000M to visit the real thing... We met the man who makes them who lives in the little house next to the shop, they are made on the premises. The other shop we really liked was the outlet of the Asociacion Indigena Red de Artesanal Productoras PUSKA, an organisation set up by women from the Altiplano villages in Chile to preserve and promote their indigenous weaving and wool-dying skills. Most items are in Alpaca wool and just really gorgeous, soft and stylish. We bought a beautiful poncho in pure white Alpaca, a scarf in dog tooth pattern (looks very English funnily enough..) and gloves. Prices utterly reasonable. If you want to support proper hand-made stuff that is local and of high quality, go there. Whilst we were there, a baptism had taken place in the Chapel on the side, and we were able to see inside, very lovely.

review_text: San Cristobal is definitely a must see for all visitors to Santiago. You can either walk up the hill (via several roads / paths) or take the tram / cable car. The summit has a beautiful statue of the Virgin Mary, which is a landmark of the city, with a great view of Santiago. In summer the view tends to be pretty clear, but the earlier you go the better as the valley is sometimes dusty / smoggy (in winter months) which makes the view less crisp / clear. You'll find several restaurants / snack bars at the top, with good views, and lots of picnic areas. In summer months there is a large public pool as well. The park connects into Parque Metropolitan de Santiago, which includes a series of trails / roads that extends across the cerros all the way to Vitacura (Americo Vespucio Norte). I run these trails with my dogs regularly and they are well-used by locals and very safe for exploring. This is my favourite park in the city of Santiago, hands down, as it is very accessible and extensive.
